newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: RTRS-Jigsaw coming together on rates - Costello.
newsitem.headline: RTRS-Jigsaw coming together on rates - Costello.

text.p: The pieces of the economic jigsaw were coming together, Australian Treasurer Peter Costello said on Friday when asked about prospects for a monetary easing.

Asked about the chances of a rate cut by Christmas, Costello said: "Well, I've made it clear that the Reserve (Bank) will make its decisions and I won't speculate on it. But from the government's point of view, we've got low inflation, we've got good wages outcomes, we've got a great budget.
"Pieces of the jigsaw are coming together, and homebuyers are now seeing the benefits of a competitive market," he said.
When a reporter suggested the bank had described wages as the only threat to lower rates, Costello said: "Well, as I have said, we've got underlying inflation right bang on target.
"We've got a good wages outcome yesterday and the pieces of the economic jigsaw are coming together and they're showing quite a nice picture," he said.
Costello spoke to reporters in Melbourne. His office issued a transcript of the news conference.
Earlier, several Australian financial institutions dropped variable home loan rates in response to expectations that the bank would soon ease monetary policy.
In July, it dropped its overnight cash rate target to 7.0 percent from 7.5 percent, the first monetary easing since a series of tightenings in 1994.
On Thursday the Bureau of Statistics said wages had grown by moderate 3.5 percent between August 1995 and August 1996.
